newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs seen on the backburner till Friday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs seen on the backburner till Friday.

text.p: Belgian government bond (OLO) traders are looking ahead to a spell of respite until Friday afternoon when key U.S. job data for February are due, they said on Wednesday, commenting on the prospects for the market.

"Until then we will stay thin and weakish," a trader said, predicting low-volume consolidation and mark-downs to attract business. A slight recovery by the Belgian franc on the mark protected the downside.
Some said today's downtick, pushing the yield on the benchmark 10-year OLO up to 5.66 percent from last night's 5.63, was exacerbated by stronger than expected German GDP data.

GDP grew by 1.4 percent in 1996 but growth stagnated in the final quarter compared to the previous quarter, the Federal Statistics Office said on Wednesday. The 1996 figure represents a slowdown from 1995 growth of 1.9 percent.
Economists had expected the 1996 growth rate to be revised down to 1.3 percent and had predicted a slight decline in fourth-quarter GDP by 0.1 or 0.2 percent from the third quarter.

Early selling pressure came in the wake of a mostly lower close for U.S. Treasuries, a trader said, noting that Tuesday's strength had been based on shaky ground since most of the buying had been done by one domestic player.
Traders said there were hardly any sellers. Domestics remained buyers on dips and could jump on the bandwaggon, provided U.S. February jobs data came out on the softish side as

Some, however, worried about an expected rebound in average hourly earnings and January consumer credit -- figures due later on Friday -- and said this could fuel fears of Fed rate hike in May. They would remain cautious until all the data were out.
They said today's second leg of Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before Congress was another excuse to remain on the sidelines.
Greenspan is expected to repeat his warnings about rapidly rising financial markets and say again a pre-emptive shot to quell any inflationary pressures might be needed.
Traders said that as along as he spoke in the same terms as he did during the first leg on February 26 there would be no upsets.
